source.title: Modeling Neural Networks with Privacy Using Neural Stochastic Differential Equations
source.authors: Sanghyun Hong; Fan Wu; Anthony Gruber; Kookjin Lee

record.file_problem: none; full paper text, including appendices, is supplied.
record.tranche_reason: Tests how neural ODE/SDE architectures and their configurations relate to training–test accuracy gaps and membership-inference risk on image benchmarks, extending generalization-gap evidence to differential-equation networks and privacy settings.
record.gate_note: The paper does not test random-label memorization or the listed optimizer, batch-size, dropout, or sharpness claims. Its own train/test accuracy and gap results, and configuration sweeps reporting these outcomes, bear on V1's broad gap relationship and V3's architecture comparison. Membership-inference attack metrics alone are not rows for the listed versions. NSDE privacy guarantees and defense comparisons without train/test gap outcomes are not included as rows. Table 12 contains configuration metrics, but the text does not connect all of those to the claim's named versions; only relevant configuration outcomes are retained.
record.test_reason: The study measures generalization gaps and membership-inference risk in NODEs and NSDEs, but tests none of V1–V8. Natural-label accuracy alone does not test V1's coexistence with random-label fitting. ResNet-14 and the compared NODEs both use convolutions, so their comparison does not test V3's convolutional-versus-fully-connected advantage. No width, optimizer, batch-size, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or memorized-example removal experiment tests the other versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors' NODE conclusions: they attribute smaller gaps and reduced membership-inference risks to constrained expressivity, while acknowledging residual risks. Their full conclusion also claims NSDE training provides privacy guarantees equivalent to DP-SGD with less utility loss, and that replacing final ResNet layers with an NSDE block reduces empirical membership risk at lower training cost. These are the authors' claims, not tests of V1–V8; 'comparable accuracy' does not mean uniformly improved test accuracy.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains and compares neural ODE/SDE architectures and reports train/test accuracy and gaps, rather than testing arbitrary-label memorization followed by natural-label generalization.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that the number of ODE blocks changes membership risk, and that NODE variants show different train–test gaps. Its NSDE block-count sweep reports accuracy changes and near-zero or negative gaps; solver choices are described as producing marginal differences in attack success.

fits_no_version.finding: NODEs have smaller train–test gaps than ResNet-14 on all four benchmarks in Table 2, but higher test accuracy only on FashionMNIST: 90.0% versus 88.4%. Their test accuracies are lower on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and TinyImageNet.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Convolutional NODE architectures can reduce train–test accuracy gaps relative to convolutional ResNets, sometimes with reduced held-out accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: SONODE and ANODE variants have smaller reported gaps and slightly higher CIFAR-10 test accuracy than ODENet-64; HBNODE has a smaller gap but lower training and test accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Changing NODE dynamics or augmenting their states can alter training fit and held-out accuracy; a smaller gap alone does not establish improved held-out performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Adding NODE blocks increases training accuracy and train–test gaps with modest test-accuracy gains. SDENet's third block reduces test accuracy from 81.91–82.42% to 74.96%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Depth and stochastic dynamics affect fit and generalization differently in NODEs and NSDEs.

fits_no_version.finding: On CIFAR-10, increasing SDENet noise from zero to σ = 2 reduces its gap from 5.16 to -0.02 percentage points while lowering test accuracy from 83.93% to 81.91%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Injected stochastic dynamics can reduce a model's train–test gap while costing held-out accuracy.

record.problems: The paper does not test random-label fitting or arbitrary-label capacity. Training method details relevant to the listed standard-gradient-method condition are not stated in the supplied text. The main architecture comparison uses different train accuracies and reports only four image benchmarks; no fully connected comparator is included. Some configuration and attack outcomes are described via figures, and the paper itself cautions that HBNODE's smaller gap may reflect lack of generalization.
record.rows_left_out: Membership-inference attack metrics, DP guarantees, and defense comparisons without corresponding train/test gap outcomes were omitted because the listed versions concern generalization behavior. Solver-sweep outcomes on attack success were also omitted. Figure-only configuration outcomes without explicit train/test accuracy or gap descriptions were not transcribed.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting capacity, coexistence with natural-label generalization under the same recipe, and chance-level held-out performance with random labels.
Test-error trends when widening beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers, local-connectivity attribution, learned sparse connections, and initialization from trained convolutional networks.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning, switching optimizers, and decoupled weight decay.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that recover large-batch performance.
Dropout's effect on held-out error, small-data and excessive-dropout regimes, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay with augmentation.
Magnitude-scaled weight-perturbation sharpness, its association with generalization gaps, and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing examples selected by label-memorization influence versus removing equally many random examples, followed by retraining.

record.verdict_notes: Discard the record's V1 and V3 verdicts. V1 is not a generic claim about generalization gaps, and 'feedforward' does not mean 'fully connected': Appendix A explicitly defines convolutional ResNet and NODE blocks. The study cites Feldman and Zhang but does not reproduce V8's removal experiment. No omitted result in the supplied text warrants a missing entry for V1–V8.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or natural-versus-random-label test comparison; no evidence that the models fit arbitrary labels.
No fully connected image-network comparator or local-connectivity isolation.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: NODE and non-stochastic variants on FashionMNIST; NODE variants on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and TinyImageNet
reader_labels.reason: The reported NODE gaps are below the ResNet-14 gaps on all four benchmarks, and selected NODE variants have smaller gaps with comparable or higher test accuracy (R2, R4, R6, R8, R16–R19).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: three-block NODE configurations and HBNODE on CIFAR-10
reader_labels.reason: Some lower gaps coincide with reduced test accuracy or the paper's stated lack of generalization; the block-count sweep also reports larger gaps as blocks increase (R19, R21, R22, R24, R25).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: NODE versus ResNet-14 across FashionMNIST, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and TinyImageNet
reader_labels.reason: NODE has lower test accuracy on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and TinyImageNet, though it has higher test accuracy on FashionMNIST; no fully connected image comparator is tested (R1–R8).
